name: Tajikistan
snapshot: Ruled since 1992 by Emomali Rahmon, who appears to be preparing his son to succeed him, in a remittance economy on the Afghan border.
culture: Tajiks speak a form of Persian, unlike their Turkic neighbours, and claim the Samanid dynasty and poets like Rudaki as their heritage. Navruz, the Persian new year, is the biggest holiday. The Pamir mountains and the Wakhan corridor are home to Ismaili Muslim communities with their own languages.
society: Tajikistan is Central Asia's poorest country, and remittances from migrant workers in Russia equal around a third of GDP. A 1992 to 1997 civil war killed tens of thousands. The government has banned the hijab and restricted religious practice. The Rogun dam, when complete, will be the world's tallest.
situation: Emomali Rahmon has ruled since 1992; a 2016 referendum lifted term limits for him and lowered the minimum age for presidents, opening the way for his son Rustam Emomali, now speaker of the upper house. Opposition parties have been banned and critics jailed, even abroad. Since late 2025, attacks from Afghan territory have killed several Chinese workers near the border, and Beijing has demanded better protection.
power: A presidential republic in form and an autocracy in practice. Rahmon rules through the presidency and his People's Democratic Party, and constitutional changes exempt him from term limits.
